accepted.s: Under Article 262(1) of the Constitution, Parliament may provide by law for the adjudication of disputes relating to which of the following?
o: Distribution of taxes between the Union and the States
Disputes concerning elections to State Legislatures
accepted.x: Article 262(1) empowers Parliament to provide by law for the adjudication of disputes relating to the use, distribution or control of waters of inter-State rivers and river valleys.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the constitutional provision with its subject.
accepted.sec: Inter-state water disputes - Art. 262, ISRWD Act, tribunals involving AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 262 of the Constitution:
1. Parliament may exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and all other courts in respect of inter-State river water disputes.
2. The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 131 includes all inter-State river water disputes.
3. The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 provides for the constitution of tribunals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Article 262(2) permits Parliament to bar the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts, and Article 131 does not cover inter-State water disputes.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the constitutional exception to Article 131.
accepted.sec: Inter-state water disputes - Art. 262, ISRWD Act, tribunals involving AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legislative position concerning inter-State rivers?
o: Water is exclusively in the Concurrent List.
Water is in the State List, while regulation and development of inter-State rivers and river valleys is in the Union List.
Water is entirely a Union List subject, including water within a State.
Both water and inter-State rivers are exclusively in the State List.
accepted.x: Water is Entry 17 of the State List, whereas regulation and development of inter-State rivers and river valleys is Entry 56 of the Union List.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed-list trap by separating general water from inter-State rivers.
accepted.sec: Inter-state water disputes - Art. 262, ISRWD Act, tribunals involving AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act and the River Boards Act were enacted in which year?
accepted.x: Both the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act and the River Boards Act were enacted in 1956.
accepted.tq: Test the exact year against nearby constitutional and legislative dates.
accepted.sec: Inter-state water disputes - Art. 262, ISRWD Act, tribunals involving AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: With reference to the River Boards Act, 1956, which of the following is correct?
o: It deals exclusively with distribution of Union taxes.
No River Board has ever been set up under the Act.
It was repealed by the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956.
It resulted in the establishment of one River Board for every inter-State river.
accepted.x: Although the River Boards Act was enacted in 1956, no River Board has ever been set up under it.
accepted.tq: Watch for the absolute-looking but source-supported institutional fact.
accepted.sec: Inter-state water disputes - Art. 262, ISRWD Act, tribunals involving AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of inter-State water dispute tribunal and States is NOT correctly matched?
o: Second Krishna — Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
First Krishna — Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Godavari — Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
accepted.x: The Vansadhara Tribunal involves Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, not Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong State in the tribunal composition rather than relying only on the tribunal name.

accepted.s: Which of the following water dispute tribunals was constituted in 1990?
accepted.x: The Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted in 1990. The Narmada Tribunal dates to 1969, Ravi-Beas to 1986 and Mahadayi to 2010.
accepted.tq: Use the year as the discriminator among closely related tribunals.
accepted.sec: Inter-state water disputes - Art. 262, ISRWD Act, tribunals involving AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following States is NOT a party to any of the Godavari, Krishna or Vansadhara tribunals listed below?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh is party to all three listed tribunals; Maharashtra is involved in the Godavari and Krishna disputes, and Odisha in the Godavari and Vansadhara disputes. Chhattisgarh is not listed in these tribunal compositions.
accepted.tq: Group the States by tribunal membership and identify the outsider.
accepted.sec: Inter-state water disputes - Art. 262, ISRWD Act, tribunals involving AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Article 261 of the Constitution provides for which of the following?
o: Uniformity of service conditions in All-India Services
Distribution of financial resources between the Union and the States
Full faith and credit throughout India to public acts, records and judicial proceedings
Adjudication of inter-State river water disputes
accepted.x: Article 261 requires full faith and credit throughout India to public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every State.
accepted.tq: Directly match the Article with its constitutional principle.
accepted.sec: Full faith and credit to public acts, records and judicial proceedings  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A final civil court judgment delivered in one State is sought to be executed in another State. Which constitutional provision facilitates this?
accepted.x: Article 261(3) provides that final judgments and orders of civil courts in any part of India may be executed anywhere within India according to law.
accepted.tq: Apply the constitutional rule to a concrete inter-State enforcement situation.
accepted.sec: Full faith and credit to public acts, records and judicial proceedings  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 261:
1. It applies to public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every State.
2. Its operation is confined to the State in which the act or record originated.
3. Final civil court judgments may be executed anywhere in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Article 261 extends the principle throughout India, so statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the territorial-limitation trap in statement 2.
accepted.sec: Full faith and credit to public acts, records and judicial proceedings  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as an All-India Service?
accepted.x: The Indian Forest Service, along with the IAS and IPS, is an All-India Service. The Indian Foreign Service and Indian Revenue Service are Central Services.
accepted.tq: Separate the similarly named Central Services from the constitutionally recognised All-India Services.
accepted.sec: All-India vs Central vs State services - classify  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Service)
 a. Indian Administrative Service
 b. Indian Police Service
 c. Indian Foreign Service
 d. State civil service

List-II (Category)
 i. State Service

accepted.x: State police services belong to the State Services category; they are not All-India Services.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong category by distinguishing State cadres from All-India cadres.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Indian Foreign Service from the Indian Forest Service?
o: The former is a Central Service and the latter is an All-India Service.
The former is an All-India Service and the latter is a Central Service.
accepted.x: The Indian Foreign Service is classified as a Central Service, whereas the Indian Forest Service is an All-India Service.
accepted.tq: Compare look-alike service names by focusing on their exact category.
accepted.sec: All-India vs Central vs State services - classify  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Satyendranath Tagore is associated with which of the following distinctions?
o: First chairperson of the Inter-State Council
First Indian to clear the ICS in 1864
First Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission in 1926
First Indian member of the Indian Forest Service
accepted.x: Satyendranath Tagore was the first Indian to clear the Indian Civil Service examination, in 1864.
accepted.tq: Match the personality with the precise first rather than a related administrative milestone.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The first Public Service Commission in India was set up on:
accepted.x: The first Public Service Commission in India was set up on 1 October 1926.
accepted.tq: Test the exact day, month and year against nearby constitutional dates.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting held in August 2026:
1. It was held on 20 August 2026 near Mamallapuram in Tamil Nadu.
2. Amit Shah chaired the meeting as Union Home Minister.
3. C. Joseph Vijay, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, was its vice-chairman.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the meeting was held near Mamallapuram on 20 August 2026, chaired by Home Minister Amit Shah, with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay as vice-chairman.
accepted.tq: Verify date, venue and office-holder separately before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh is included in which Zonal Council and is party to which combination of water tribunals?
o: Southern Zonal Council; Godavari, Krishna and Vansadhara
Eastern Zonal Council; Narmada, Cauvery and Ravi-Beas
Southern Zonal Council; Ravi-Beas, Cauvery and Mahadayi
Central Zonal Council; Godavari, Narmada and Mahadayi
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh belongs to the Southern Zonal Council and is party to the Godavari, Krishna and Vansadhara water dispute tribunals.
accepted.tq: Combine the regional classification with the State’s specific tribunal relationships.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Mullaperiyar dam, constructed in 1895, is located in which State and operated by which State?
accepted.x: The Mullaperiyar dam is located in Kerala, while it is operated by Tamil Nadu. The dam dates from 1895.
accepted.tq: Separate location from operational control, a common inter-State trap.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: In the Mullaperiyar matter, the Supreme Court-directed Supervisory Committee involves which authority under the Dam Safety Act, 2021?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court-directed Supervisory Committee in the Mullaperiyar matter involves the National Dam Safety Authority under the Dam Safety Act, 2021.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact statutory authority instead of substituting a related water institution.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The proposed amendment to the IAS Cadre Rules concerning unilateral central deputation has been criticised primarily because it may:
o: transfer the power of judicial review to the Union
remove the distinction between Central and State Lists
harm the morale of State bureaucracies
accepted.x: The criticism is that unilateral central deputation may adversely affect the morale of State bureaucracies. It does not abolish State services or alter the legislative lists.
accepted.tq: Match the policy criticism with its stated administrative consequence.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following has been identified as a proposed role for the Inter-State Council in relation to legislation?
o: Approving every Money Bill before Parliament
Serving as a permanent screening body for Bills affecting the Concurrent List
Replacing the Supreme Court in all federal disputes
accepted.x: A proposal is to make the Inter-State Council a permanent screening body for Bills that affect the Concurrent List.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a proposed coordination role from constitutionally assigned judicial or recruitment functions.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Mahanadi water dispute currently referred to in the context of inter-State relations is between:
accepted.x: The Mahanadi dispute is between Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
accepted.tq: Use the river-dispute pair as the direct identifying feature.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following is identified as a continuing concern regarding the functioning of the Inter-State Council?
o: It meets too frequently and duplicates every State Cabinet.
It meets rarely, limiting its effectiveness as a forum of coordination.
It is composed exclusively of judges of the Supreme Court.
It has jurisdiction only over municipal elections.
accepted.x: The Inter-State Council has been criticised for meeting rarely; proposals seek to strengthen its role in Centre-State coordination.
accepted.tq: Select the institutional criticism that directly relates to the body’s functioning.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the present relevance of the CAPF issue mentioned in the context of administrative services?
o: A dispute over service status and a proposed Central Armed Forces Bill
A dispute regarding the constitutional validity of the Concurrent List
A proposal to abolish the Indian Police Service
A proposal to merge all State police forces into the Army
accepted.x: The current issue concerns the service status of CAPF personnel and a proposed Central Armed Forces Bill.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise pair of issues instead of choosing broader but unsupported reforms.
